zichtbaarheid.stavenHint: Show members and their system lines.
zichtbaarheid.profielKleurHint: Each section its own colour, with a legend on the canvas. Selection takes precedence; in 3D so does the unity check colouring.
zichtbaarheid.platenHint: Show plate geometry and plate contours.
zichtbaarheid.meshHint: Show the element layout of the plates (the analysis mesh).
zichtbaarheid.belastingenHint: Show all load arrows and load surfaces.
zichtbaarheid.spoorHint: Object tracking while drawing in 3D: rest the mouse on a node or beam to acquire it; tracking lines along the axes in the work plane, their intersections, extension, perpendicular and parallel. Alt turns all snaps off temporarily, Shift keeps the direction along an axis.
zichtbaarheid.hoekHint: Angle snap while drawing a member: if the direction is within the tolerance of 0° or 90°, it is set exactly to that angle; the length stays the same. A node or grid line takes precedence.
zichtbaarheid.hoekTolerantieHint: How many degrees the direction may deviate: 0.1 to 15. Comma or point allowed.
zichtbaarheid.hoekExtraHint: The angle snap then also catches 30°, 45° and 60° and their mirror images.
zichtbaarheid.verbindingsTolerantieHint: Within this distance a node counts as “on the member” or “at the same place” as another node: the model check reports it, and a new node is connected or reused. 0.1 to 25 mm, default 5. Comma or point allowed. Existing nodes are not moved; a new node on a member is placed on the member axis.
zichtbaarheid.knopenAansluitenHint: 3D only. When a point lies within the connection tolerance of an existing node after drawing, inserting, moving or copying, it becomes that node (merged). When a node then lies on a member, or a new member runs through an existing node, the member is split there. In the same undo step, with a message. Connecting also happens after importing a model. An opened project does not change by itself: the model check on the canvas reports such nodes, with the Merge and Connect buttons.
zichtbaarheid.verbindingsTolerantieHint3d: Within this distance of the member axis a node counts as ‘on the member’, and within this distance of another node as ‘at the same place’: the model check reports it, Connect nodes splits the member there and Merge nodes makes them one node (also automatically). 0.1 to 25 mm, default 5; the same setting as in 2D. A node within this distance of a member end, measured along the member axis, does not count as ‘on the member’. The node is not moved: the parts of the member run to the node.
zichtbaarheid.knoopnummersHint: The number next to each node.
zichtbaarheid.staafnummersHint: The member number, e.g. (3), at mid-member next to the section name — as in the structural sketch of the report.
zichtbaarheid.lastWaardenHint: The numbers at the loads (kN, kN/m, kNm, ΔT). The arrows remain.
zichtbaarheid.peilmatenHint: The level mark of each level (+5.00 m). Click a level mark to change the height of the level.
zichtbaarheid.maatlijnenHint: The dimensions between grid axes and levels (mm).
zichtbaarheid.aanzichtBreedteHint: The section width b as a label at the elevation: the elevation shows the depth h, the width is perpendicular to the drawing.
zichtbaarheid.supportScaleHint: Display only; analysis restraints remain unchanged.
zichtbaarheid.scharnierenHint: The hinges and springs at the member ends.
zichtbaarheid.stramienProject: Belongs to the project (also in the Grids and levels panel).
zichtbaarheid.alleenMetAanzicht: Visible once the elevation is on.
zichtbaarheid.resultatenNoot: The same switches as in the explorer, Results tab.
zichtbaarheid.onthouden: Labels and geometry are remembered for you, not in the project.

wind.gevelhoogteHint: Roof without walls: the walls are not in the model. Enter the height of the underside of the roof above ground; the building height becomes wall + roof.
wind.formHint: Canopy, carport or open shed without walls — EN 1991-1-4 §7.3.
wind.blockageHint: φ = 0: nothing under the roof. φ = 1: fully blocked at the leeward side, e.g. by stored timber, goods or parked cars. In between: the blocked part of the cross-section under the roof.
wind.canopyDirections: c_p,net and c_f apply to all wind directions (§7.3(3)); c_pi does not apply. Empty h = the height of the model.
wind.canopyExtraHint: Friction and wind on columns form one horizontal load case per wind direction. A row of multibay duopitch canopies gets ψ_mc from table 7.8; the position counts from one end, the generator counts from both ends as in figure 7.18. b = column width perpendicular to the wind, d = depth in the wind direction.
wind.slopedRoofShort: Read c_pe,10 from table 7.4a (and 7.4b for perpendicular wind) at this roof pitch.
wind.title: Wind load generator — NEN-EN 1991-1-4 + Dutch NA
wind.qpManual: Enter manually (e.g. from the NA table)
wind.qpManualSourcePlaceholder: E.g. project calculation, table and edition
wind.cpiManualSourcePlaceholder: E.g. opening calculation, document and edition
wind.positionHint: Load width = spacing (internal frame) or spacing/2 (gable frame); override it below when it differs.
wind.distanceHint: Determines whether the frame falls in edge zone F/A (closer than e/4 resp. e/5 to the gable) — see EN 1991-1-4 fig. 7.5 and 7.6.
wind.slopedRoofHint: This generator does not fill in table 7.4a/7.4b itself. Read c_pe,10 for your roof pitch and enter the values here; without them the generator refuses a model with a pitched roof.
wind.summaryGeometry: Height h = {{h}} m · span d = {{d}} m · h/d = {{hd}} · load width = {{b}} m
wind.statusActive: Tracking the structure — {{runs}} runs, {{applied}} applied, {{skipped}} unchanged.

nonlinear.missingSecondOrder: The second-order state is missing from the results; the calculation was not carried out.

creep.title: Calculated without creep
creep.noCoefficient_one: No creep coefficient φ(∞,t₀) has been specified for member {{ids}} (art. 3.1.4), so φ_ef = 0 was used.
creep.noCoefficient_other: No creep coefficient φ(∞,t₀) has been specified for members {{ids}} (art. 3.1.4), so φ_ef = 0 was used.
creep.slsTooSmall: The {{aantal}} SLS combination(s) therefore give a deflection that is TOO SMALL.
creep.determinate: The structure is statically determinate, so the force distribution itself does not change.
creep.indeterminate: The structure is not demonstrably statically determinate ({{toelichting}}), so the FORCE DISTRIBUTION is also incorrect: overly stiff concrete members attract too much moment.
creep.fillIn: Enter φ(∞,t₀) in the project settings or per member in the §5.8 data.

projectSettingsDialog.effectChecked: Listed in the report: checks have been run to this standard.
projectSettingsDialog.effectCheckedOverruled: Listed in the report anyway: checks have been run to this standard. A completed check is a fact about the calculation, not a preference; your choice applies again once those check results are gone.
projectSettingsDialog.effectOn: Listed in the report, even while the model does not yet contain any {{materiaal}}.
projectSettingsDialog.effectOff: Not listed in the report, even if the model contains {{materiaal}}.
projectSettingsDialog.effectModel: Listed in the report as soon as the model contains {{materiaal}} or checks have been run for it — otherwise not.
projectSettingsDialog.standardsExplanation: This choice only determines what the report lists under the basis of design; it does not change the calculation. By default each standard follows the model, so a purely steel calculation does not mention timber. Set a standard to “Always list” if you are anticipating what you are still going to draw — “Follows the model” reverses that choice.
projectSettingsDialog.onlyDutchAnnex: This edition only contains design values for the Dutch national annex.
projectSettingsDialog.designLifeClass2: Category 2 — 10 to 25 years: replaceable structural parts
projectSettingsDialog.designLifeClass3: Category 3 — 15 to 30 years: agricultural and similar structures
projectSettingsDialog.designLifeClass4: Category 4 — 50 years: building structures and other common structures
projectSettingsDialog.designLifeClass5: Category 5 — 100 years: monumental buildings, bridges and infrastructure
projectSettingsDialog.consequenceExplainIntro: The consequence class determines the partial factors of the default load combinations according to NEN-EN 1990 {{bron}}:
projectSettingsDialog.consequenceExplainTail: ; this factor is not applied again to any result. A combination you have modified or added yourself does not follow the consequence class.
projectSettingsDialog.windExplainRegion: Wind region {{gebied}} gives a basic wind velocity
projectSettingsDialog.windExplainNationalAnnex: from the terrain type table of the national annex. If you use that table, enter the peak velocity pressure manually in the wind load generator.

loadValue.lineNone: Line load {{last}} on member {{staaf}} has no value. Enter `q` (uniformly distributed, kN/m) or `qStart` and `qEnd` (trapezoidal).
loadValue.lineNoneWrongField: Line load {{last}} on member {{staaf}} has no value: {{velden}} is not read for a line load. Enter `q` (uniformly distributed, kN/m) or `qStart` and `qEnd` (trapezoidal).
loadValue.lineHalf: Line load {{last}} on member {{staaf}} has `{{heeft}}` but no `{{mist}}` (and no `q` to fall back on). Enter `{{mist}}`; for a uniform load only `q`.
loadValue.lineWrongField: Line load {{last}} on member {{staaf}}: {{velden}} is not read for a line load and would be lost. Enter a point load or moment as a separate load.
loadValue.lineRange: Line load {{last}} on member {{staaf}}: the loaded part does not start before its end (startFrac {{begin}}, endFrac {{einde}}). An empty or reversed part is not a load and would be lost. Enter 0 ≤ startFrac < endFrac ≤ 1, measured from the start node.
loadValue.momentNone: Moment {{last}} on node {{knoop}} has no value. A moment is entered in `my` (kNm).
loadValue.momentWrongField: Moment {{last}} on node {{knoop}} has no value in `my`: {{velden}} is not read for a moment. A moment is entered in `my` (kNm).
loadValue.momentExtraField: Moment {{last}} on node {{knoop}}: {{velden}} is not read for a moment and would be lost. Enter a force as a separate point load.
loadValue.forceNone: Point load {{last}} has no value. Enter `fz` (vertical) and/or `fx` (horizontal), in kN.
loadValue.forceWrongField: Point load {{last}} has no value in `fx` or `fz`: `my` is not read for a point load. A moment is a separate load (pointMoment).
loadValue.forceExtraField: Point load {{last}}: `my` is not read for a point load and would be lost. A moment is a separate load (pointMoment).

plateEdge.openingOnPerimeterRoute: the load is on the edge of an opening (`openingId`), but it is read here by a route that only knows the perimeter of the plate. Please report this: the address is deliberately rejected rather than silently placed on the perimeter.
plateEdge.nameAndIndex: the load specifies both a named edge (`edge`) and an edge index (`edgeIndex`). Give only one: with two addresses it cannot be said which edge is meant and from which corner the positions are measured.
plateEdge.noEdge: the load specifies no edge. Give `edgeIndex` (edge i runs from corner i to corner i+1) or, for an axis-aligned rectangle, `edge`.
plateEdge.plateTooFewCorners: the plate has {{n}} corners; an edge only exists from three corners.
plateEdge.indexMissing: edge index {{i}} does not exist: the plate has {{n}} edges (edgeIndex 0 to {{max}}).
plateEdge.diagonal: edge {{rand}} (edgeIndex {{i}}, corner {{van}} → corner {{naar}}) does not run along the perimeter: the corners of this rectangle are not in perimeter order, so this pair of corners is a diagonal. Choose the edge with a named edge (`edge`) or redraw the plate in perimeter order.
plateEdge.unknownName: "{{edge}}" is not a named edge. Allowed: {{lijst}}.
plateEdge.nameOnPolygon: a named edge ("{{naam}}") only exists on an axis-aligned rectangle; this plate has {{n}} corners that do not form an axis-aligned rectangle and is analysed as a polygon. Choose the edge again with an edge index (`edgeIndex`: edge i runs from corner i to corner i+1).
plateEdge.openingAndName: the load specifies both an opening (`openingId`) and a named edge (`edge`). An opening has no named edges; choose the edge with `edgeIndex` (edge j runs from opening corner j to corner j+1).
plateEdge.openingIdNotInteger: `openingId` {{opening}} is not an integer; give the id of an opening of this plate.
plateEdge.plateHasNoOpenings: the load is on opening {{opening}}, but this plate has no openings.
plateEdge.openingMissing: opening {{opening}} does not exist on this plate. Present: {{lijst}}.
plateEdge.openingDuplicate: opening {{opening}} occurs {{aantal}} times on this plate; the address is therefore ambiguous. Give each opening its own id.
plateEdge.openingTooFewCorners: opening {{opening}} has {{n}} corners; an edge only exists from three corners.
plateEdge.openingNoEdge: the load specifies opening {{opening}} but none of its edges. Give `edgeIndex` (edge j runs from opening corner j to corner j+1; 0 to {{max}}).
plateEdge.openingIndexMissing: edge index {{i}} does not exist on opening {{opening}}: that opening has {{n}} edges (edgeIndex 0 to {{max}}).
plateEdge.openingEdgeZero: edge {{rand}} of opening {{opening}} has a length of {{lengte}} mm and cannot carry a load.

plateLoad.plateMissing: {{soort}} {{last}} is on plate {{plaat}}, but that plate does not exist.
plateLoad.pointNoPosition: Point load {{last}} on plate {{plaat}} has no position along the edge. Enter the distance from the start corner.

uitgezet.verwijderd: Load case “{{naam}}” carried the automatic self-weight and has been removed. Self-weight is now OFF and is no longer included. Switch “Self-weight” back on to include it in the first permanent load case.

eigenGewicht.geenHandmatigeLast: Load case “{{naam}}” is filled automatically with the self-weight; no load can be entered in it. Select another load case first.
eigenGewicht.aanbodTitel: Self-weight in its own load case?
eigenGewicht.aanbod: This project includes the self-weight in the first permanent load case, among the entered loads. Nothing has been converted: the project calculates exactly as before. You can add the “Self-weight” case and move the self-weight there; the combination results do not change.
eigenGewicht.verplaatst: The “Self-weight” load case has been added and now carries the self-weight. Ctrl+Z undoes this in one step.

loadCases.modelTabTitle: Model view — show structure only, no loads
loadCases.listTitle: All load cases — pick one directly
loadCases.selfWeightTitle: Include self-weight (ρ·A·g): generated automatically in the “Self-weight” load case, or — in an older project without that case — in the first permanent load case
loadCases.selfWeightCaseHint: This case is filled automatically with the self-weight (q = ρ·A·g per member). Deleting it or changing its type switches self-weight off.
loadCases.selfWeightOfferTitle: Self-weight currently sits among the loads of the first permanent load case. Add the “Self-weight” case and move the self-weight there. The combination results do not change; one step, undo with Ctrl+Z.

analysisDescription.eersteOrde: First order, linear: each combination is the weighted sum of the load cases.
analysisDescription.tweedeOrdeGeometrisch: Second order, geometrically non-linear (P-Δ): each combination is solved separately with factored loads and geometric stiffness.
analysisDescription.tweedeOrdeFysisch: Second order, geometrically and materially non-linear: as P-Δ, but the concrete members get the secant EI per segment from the calculation engine (NEN-EN 1992-1-1 5.8.6). Without concrete members with a reinforcement cage the result equals 2nd order (P-Δ).
analysisDescription.axiaalFysischRust: Experimental Rust analysis: P-Δ with axial steel plasticity or concrete tensile damage over a load path. Bending stays elastic; code checks are not run.

loadCases.axialPathHint: Absolute load factors, for example 1, 0, 0.5 for loading, unloading and reloading.
loadCases.axialPathError: Enter 1 to 100 finite load factors separated by commas.
loadCases.segmentTitle: Target segment length in mm. Each concrete member is split into segments of equal length, each with its own secant EI (5.8.6(6)). Shorter = more accurate and slower; the application does not coarsen on its own.
loadCases.creepTitle: Final value of the creep coefficient φ(∞,t₀) according to art. 3.1.4, for every concrete member without its own value in the §5.8 data. The engine applies it according to 5.8.6(4) — all design values times (1 + φ_ef) — which for the initial slope amounts to E_c,eff = E_cm/(1 + φ) of (7.20). EMPTY = not specified: the analysis then runs WITHOUT creep, the deflection comes out too small and that is the unsafe side. Tick the box next to it to have φ(∞,t₀) calculated according to annex B; a value specified here takes precedence.
loadCases.creepFeedsBoth: This value feeds two calculations: the SLS stiffness in the physically non-linear analysis (5.8.6(4)) and the column check in every analysis type (A in λ_lim per 5.8.3.1(1), φ_ef per (5.19)). A member with its own φ(∞,t₀) in the §5.8 data takes precedence.
loadCases.noConcreteBarsTitle: Material non-linearity applies to concrete members with a reinforcement cage: material a strength class (e.g. C30/37), section a rectangle (e.g. 300x500) and a cage in the member properties. Without such members the result equals 2nd order (P-Δ).
loadCases.swayTitle: Include sway imperfection (initial imperfection): each vertical load gets a horizontal companion H = φ·V. Choose where φ comes from next to this — the fixed denominator (the basic value, and the setting of every existing project) or the code formula of EN 1993-1-1 (5.5), EN 1992-1-1 (5.1) or EN 1995-1-1 (5.1).
loadCases.tensionOnlyFitTitle: Tension-only members fitted after the permanent load: their stress-free length follows the deformation under the permanent load cases (factor 1.0, including self-weight and load panels). Under that load alone they then carry nothing; whatever comes after, they do carry.
loadCases.crossRuleTitle: Cross rule: of two tension-only members that cross each other, the one with the largest axial force always stays active, even if it carries a small compressive force. A bay thus keeps its bracing when the columns shorten under vertical load.
loadCases.swaySourceTitle:
Where φ comes from.

fixed denominator — the number entered, without α_h and α_m. This is the basic value of the code and thus the safe upper bound; it is also the setting of every project created before this choice existed.
EN 1993-1-1 (5.5) — φ = φ₀·α_h·α_m with φ₀ = 1/200 (steel).
EN 1992-1-1 (5.1) — θ_i = θ₀·α_h·α_m with θ₀ = 1/300 according to the Dutch national annex (concrete).
EN 1995-1-1 (5.1) — φ = 0.005 for h ≤ 5 m, otherwise 0.005·√(5/h); no α_m (timber).
most unfavourable — evaluates all codes applicable to this model and takes the largest φ.
loadCases.swayHeightTitle: Height h in mm for α_h = 2/√(h/1000). Empty = derived from the model ({{hoogte}} mm): from the lowest support to the top of the structure (EN 1993-1-1 figure 5.2; EN 1992-1-1 §5.2(6) for the bracing structure).
loadCases.swayMembersTitle: Number of load-bearing vertical members m for α_m = √(0.5(1+1/m)). Empty = derived from the model ({{aantal}}): the number of column lines, where members stacked on top of each other form one column. The 50 % criterion of EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(3)a cannot be applied here (it requires the column forces, which only follow from the analysis); remove a lightly loaded post manually — smaller m gives larger φ.
loadCases.swayDirectionTitle: Direction of the equivalent horizontal forces: BOTH. Each combination is analysed with the sway imperfection in +x and in −x (EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(2): in the most unfavourable direction); the envelope and the code check take, per member, the more unfavourable of the two, and the combination name states the direction. The preferred direction stored here ({{richting}}) only determines which variant keeps the original combination number.
loadCases.name: Name
loadCases.categoryTitle: Category of use according to NEN-EN 1990 NB table NB.2–A1.1 — only for variable loads
loadCases.deleteCaseTitle: Delete load case, all its loads and its factor in every combination
loadCases.atLeastOneCase: At least one load case is required.
loadCases.deleteCaseConfirm: Delete "{{naam}}"? All loads in this case will also be deleted, and its factor disappears from every combination.
loadCases.casesHintBeforeGamma: A new case has type “Other” and only counts once you give it a type: the standard combinations then include it (permanent → γ
loadCases.casesHintAfterGamma: , variable, snow and wind → its own turn as leading load and ψ as accompanying load). Each variable case appears in combinations with and without that case: a variable load only counts where it acts unfavourably (free action, NEN-EN 1991-1-1 6.2.1(1)P), so that a floor load divided per span can also be on a single span. The factors follow NEN-EN 1990 {{bron}} and table NB.2–A1.1.
loadCases.undoReplaceTitle: Restore the combinations as they were in the project file
loadCases.replaceConfirm: Replace all combinations (except those of the wind generator) with the standard set? Your own combinations will be lost.
loadCases.originTitle: Standard = derived from the cases and the consequence class; custom = created or modified by you
loadCases.combosHint: Standard combinations are derived from the load cases and consequence class {{klasse}} (γ from NEN-EN 1990 {{bron}}, ψ from table NB.2–A1.1) and are updated when you add cases, change their type or delete them; the combinations of the wind generator are updated in the same way. If you change a factor, name or type, it becomes a custom combination: the app no longer adjusts it, but does check it after every change. When opening a project of version 0.3.11 or older, the app replaces the old standard combinations with this set, with a notice and Undo; custom combinations are kept. Factor 0 (or empty) = that load case does not take part in this combination. A negative factor is allowed — for example
loadCases.creepAnnexBTitle: Have φ(∞,t₀) calculated per concrete member according to EN 1992-1-1 annex B (B.1–B.9), from the relative humidity RH, the age t₀ at loading and the cement class (S slow, N normal, R rapid hardening). The notional size h₀ = 2·A_c/u follows from the cross-section of each member, with the whole perimeter taken as drying. A specified φ(∞,t₀) takes precedence, and the value in the §5.8 data of a member takes precedence over that. Not included: the temperature correction (B.10) and non-linear creep for a compressive stress above 0.45·f_ck(t₀) (3.1.4(4)). The derivation is shown in the report with the concrete member.
loadCases.creepAnnexBOverridden: A φ(∞,t₀) has been specified; it takes precedence and this annex B input is not used. Clear the φ box to use the calculated value.
loadCases.creepAnnexBFailedTitle: Creep coefficient according to annex B not determined
loadCases.creepAnnexBFailedBody: Member {{staaf}}: {{reden}} This member is analysed without a creep coefficient.

swayDerivation.footLowestNode: no supports in the model, so the lowest node, z = {{z}} mm
swayDerivation.heightDerivation: h = {{h}} m — from the base ({{voet}}) to the top of the structure (z = {{top}} mm). EN 1993-1-1 figure 5.2 measures h from the support level; EN 1992-1-1 §5.2(6) calls it the height of the building for the bracing structure.
swayDerivation.membersFallback: m = 1 (fallback) — this model contains no member steeper than {{graden}}° to the horizontal, so there is no column line to count. m = 1 gives α_m = 1.00: the largest value the formula can take, and therefore the safe fallback.
swayDerivation.membersDerived_one: m = {{count}} — {{count}} column line: {{lijst}}. A member counts as vertical from {{graden}}° to the horizontal; members that share a node together form one column, so a column through several storeys counts once.
swayDerivation.membersDerived_other: m = {{count}} — {{count}} column lines: {{lijst}}. A member counts as vertical from {{graden}}° to the horizontal; members that share a node together form one column, so a column through several storeys counts once.
swayDerivation.membersNote50Percent: NOTE on m: EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(3)a only counts columns carrying at least 50 % of the average vertical column force. Those forces follow from the analysis and the analysis needs φ, so that criterion is not applied here — all column lines count. A lightly loaded post should be removed manually: smaller m gives larger α_m and thus larger φ, the safe side.
swayDerivation.wallsNotCounted: Shear walls do not count in m: a wall usually braces rather than being braced, and counting it would raise m and lower φ. If a wall does carry vertical load here, raise m manually.

base.en1993: φ₀ is the basic value: φ₀ = 1/200.
base.en1992: θ₀ is the basic value. The Dutch national annex strikes out the recommended EN value 1/200 and prescribes 1/300.
base.en1995: φ = 0.005 rad for h ≤ 5 m; this code has no separate basic value.

en1995.h: the height of the structure or the length of the member, in m.
en1995.phiUpTo5: h ≤ 5 m, so φ = 0.005 rad. This code has no α_m and no lower limit on the height reduction.

h.en1992: l is the height of the building; §5.2(6), case 'effect on the bracing system'.
h.en1993: h is the height of the structure, in metres (figure 5.2).

alphaH.upper: α_h = 2/√h = 2/√{{h}} and is limited by the upper limit 1.0.
alphaH.lower: α_h = 2/√h = 2/√{{h}} and is limited by the lower limit 2/3.

m.en1992: m is the number of vertical members contributing to the horizontal force on the bracing system.
m.en1993: m is the number of columns in a row (only those with N_Ed ≥ 50 % of the average).

swayDerivation.fixedExplain: Fixed denominator from the project settings; the reduction factors α_h and α_m of the code are NOT applied. This is the basic value and therefore the safe upper bound.

warn.notDerivable: h and/or m cannot be derived from the model (no vertical member, or no height). Check them and enter them yourself if necessary.
warn.noHeight: The structure has no height, so α_h takes its upper limit 1.0. A sway imperfection on a flat model is a choice of the user, not a code requirement.
warn.noNormApplies: None of the three codes applies to this model (all members have a free or unknown material). The fixed denominator remains in force: φ = 1/{{noemer}}.
warn.normWithoutMaterial: {{norm}} is selected, but this model contains no material covered by that code (it does contain: {{wel}}).

heading.fixed: Sway imperfection: fixed denominator from the project settings.

swayDerivation.directionBoth: Direction: both. Each load combination is analysed with the sway imperfection in +x and in −x, as two variants with the direction in the name; the envelope and the code check take, per member, the more unfavourable of the two (EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(2): the imperfection in the most unfavourable direction; 5.3.2(8): in all relevant directions, one at a time).
swayDerivation.directions3d: In 3D the sway imperfection acts per ULS combination in four directions, one at a time: +X, −X, +Y and −Y (EN 1993-1-1 §5.3.2(8)). Every vertical load V receives a horizontal load φ·V at its own point of application (§5.3.2(7)). SLS combinations are calculated without sway imperfection.

loadCases.swayDirectionTitle3d: The sway imperfection acts in every ULS combination in turn in +X, −X, +Y and −Y (EN 1993-1-1 §5.3.2(8)); SLS combinations are calculated without it.

tree.rowDeflectionHint: Deformed shape — Hermite curve of nodal displacements
tree.rowMomentHint: Bending moment about y-axis (sagging+) perpendicular to the beam
tree.rowShearHint: Shear force in z-direction — linearly varying under UDL
tree.rowRotationHint: Rotation θ(x) = dw/dx along the member, in mrad — positive counter-clockwise; equal to the nodal rotation at a rigid connection, jumps at a hinge
tree.rowReactionsHint: Support reactions — Fx + Fz arrows at supports
tree.rowUnityCheckHint: Governing UC per member from the code check — green ≤ 1.0, red > 1.0; click a badge for the check
tree.rowEIHint: Bending stiffness EI per member segment from the materially non-linear second-order analysis; the dashed line is the uncracked EI₀, so the drop due to cracking becomes visible
tree.rowEIDisabled: No segment stiffnesses in this result — run a materially non-linear analysis (concrete) to see the cracking pattern.
tree.rowProfileNameHint: Section name in small print along each member on the canvas
tree.rowAanzichtHint: Members at true size: section depth, flanges, laminations and reinforcement around the system line. Only in the model view and the load cases, never over the result diagrams
tree.rowKipsteunenHint: Lateral restraints as symbols along the member, per flange; select or hover a member for the segment lengths in mm
tree.rowPlateStressHint: Stress contours on the plate elements — component selectable, legend on the canvas
tree.scaleTitle: Scale factor — adjust the visual size of this diagram
tree.nodeValuesTitle: Show the displacement ux / uz in mm at each node
tree.badgesAppearTitle: The badges appear as soon as the code check has results
tree.checkFailed: The check failed — see the Check tab for the reason.
tree.plateComponentTitle: Choose the stress component for the contour fills; 'mesh' shows the element edges
tree.reactionComponentsTitle: Choose which reaction components are shown; in envelope view the labels show min…max over all combinations
tree.signConventionTitle: Shear signs in the shear force diagram and bending signs in the bending moment diagram — the arc bulges towards the tension side, the two arrows show the sense of shear
tree.clickCalculateAfter: in the 2D tab to show diagrams.
tree.replacedOnOpen: Replaced on opening — review or undo

waterAccumulatie.title: Ponding · 2D beam strip
waterAccumulatie.intro: Iterative calculation of water depth and deflection for a single simply supported roof beam.
waterAccumulatie.introBeam: Length and bending stiffness of member {{id}} have been filled in.
waterAccumulatie.waterLevel: Water level above left roof edge
waterAccumulatie.lowStiffnessNote: Stiffness ratio ≤ 1: this equilibrium at the entered level can exist with a roof slope or a partly dry roof. The maximum water level has not yet been determined by this; for that, the water volume must be increased step by step.
waterAccumulatie.unstableNote: The iteration at a fixed water level does not converge. This does not yet demonstrate instability; check stiffness, camber and slope with a volume-controlled calculation. The intermediate values are not a design result.
waterAccumulatie.profileAria: Water depth along the 2D roof beam
waterAccumulatie.modelNote: Model: a single roof strip with simply supported ends; the water level stays fixed at the entered height. This is a calculation, not yet an NPR 6703 code check or drainage check. {{n}} iterations.
waterAccumulatie.sourcesNote: The volume-controlled method is not yet included in this calculation.
